messages:
alex: heads-up — seeing a cluster of nodes (gnode-143, gnode-147) enter readonly NVMe during nightly batch runs, starts ~02:05 UTC. dmesg shows "nvme nvme0: I/O 4096 QID 0 timeout" and filesystem remounts. Anyone else?
sana: saw similar alerts in eu-west2 around the same window. spikes in iops then scrub kicked in and devices remounted ro. suspect cleaner + heavy GPU aggregation.
jack: can you paste the dmesg snippet?
alex: here's a small excerpt we captured:
```
[  602.123456] nvme nvme1: queued 256s, cmd 0 qid 0 timeout
[  602.123789] nvme nvme1: controller fatal error, resetting
[  603.001234] EXT4-fs error (device nvme1n1p1): ext4_listxattr: IO failure
[  603.002345] Remounting filesystem read-only
```
irina: that looks like scanlock starvation in the ephemeral-cleaner loop. Cleaner tries to scrub ranges while a batch job saturates qdepth; we've seen that pattern when scrubers run concurrently with heavy write bursts.
sana: what scrub config were those nodes running? i thought we bumped concurrency to 4 in us-west, but eu-west might still be at 2.
jack: confirmed — eu-west2 nodes are still on scrub_concurrency=2. can we make the cleaner use adaptive backoff when nvme_cmd_timeouts spike?
paul: cost note — increasing scrub concurrency reduces time-to-clean but raises background IO and wear. There's a tradeoff vs adding more nodes. For immediate relief, tuning backoff and iops caps seems cheaper than adding capacity.
sre-bot: alert: gnode-147 remounted read-only at 2412345678. action: isolated from scheduler.
alex: i reproduced locally by running fio 4k randwrite with qdepth=128 while running the scrub loop; controller reset in ~3 minutes.
sana: proposal: (1) set scrub_concurrency=1 for eu-west2 during 02:00-04:00 UTC window, (2) add an iops_cgroup cap for the cleaner at 2000 iops, (3) make the scheduler avoid packing large job batches to single nodes during maintenance windows.
irina: +1 for the iops_cgroup. Also add a node-exporter metric nvme_cmd_timeout_count so we can alert before remount.
jack: I'll prepare a quick rollout: scrub-daemon config with iops throttle and exponential backoff. gate by image version rwinf-node-2026-03-15.
alex: that image is available and tested.
paul: note on tradeoffs — throttling cleaner may increase uncollected ephemeral data temporarily, affecting wear calculations later. Recommend time-windowed throttle and only on nodes with >70% iops util.
sana: will run a canary to 10 nodes first, monitor nvme_timeouts and scheduler evict rate for 2h.
irina: also add an alert: nvme_readonly_remounts > 1 in 1h => P0.
jack: PR created: https://git.redwood/infra/ephemeral-cleaner/compare/ef3a2 — adds backoff + iops cgroup. kicking canary to eu-west2 now.
sre-bot: deploy started: scrub-daemon canary eu-west2 (10 nodes).
sana: dashboards updated to show nvme_cmd_timeout_count and scrub_iops charts.
paul: if canary looks good, plan wider rollout at 04:30 UTC; if not, revert and schedule node reprovisioning overnight.
jack: canary green after ~45m — nvme timeouts dropped to 0 and no new readonly remounts during the window.
alex: great. follow-up: open ticket to evaluate NVMe firmware differences across vendors; we saw firmware quirks in older fleets. filing CH-4857.
irina: noted. thanks team :thumbsup:
